about.heroSubtitle: Content App is a quiet corner of the internet — no ads, no tracking, no algorithmic noise. Just carefully chosen stories in English and Bengali, built to be read, understood, and remembered.
about.whyStartedP1: The web has become loud. Every article is wrapped in autoplay videos, pop-ups, cookie banners, and three different ad networks. We got tired of it — so we built something else.
about.whyStartedP2Before: Content App started as a small experiment in
about.whyStartedP2After: what if reading could feel calm again? What if stories respected your attention, and what if bilingual readers didn't have to choose between languages?
about.whyStartedP3After: a small team based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. We're not a startup chasing scale — we're readers who wanted a better reading experience and decided to make one.
about.whyStartedP4: This isn't a product. It's a project. It exists because people show up to read, give feedback, and occasionally help cover hosting costs. If you find something useful here, that means we did our job.

simple.title: A quiet place to read, in two languages
simple.intro: Content App is a bilingual reading and research platform built for people who want to read deeply, not scroll endlessly. It works in English and Bengali, with native text-to-speech, saved favorites, and no advertising at all.
simple.whyP1: Most reading apps treat language as an afterthought. They are English-first, with Bengali content crammed in as a translation. Or they are Bengali-only, with no bridge to global research. We wanted something that treated both languages as equals — a place where a Bengali essay and an English paper sit side by side, with the same care.
simple.whyP2: We also wanted listening to be first-class. Reading is wonderful, but sometimes you want to listen while walking, cooking, or resting your eyes. Every article on Content App can be read aloud with the native text-to-speech engine of your device — free, offline, and private.
simple.what1: Read original English and Bengali articles on culture, technology, and ideas
simple.what2: Listen to any article with native text-to-speech, in either language
simple.what3: Save favorites and track your reading progress
simple.what4: Browse by topic — from history to science to literature
simple.what5: Switch between English and Bengali without losing your place
simple.principleFree: no paywall, no subscription, no hidden costs
simple.principlePrivate: no ads, no trackers, no third-party analytics
simple.principleBilingual: English and Bengali designed as equals, not translations of each other
simple.principleAccessible: read, listen, or both — in whichever language you think in
simple.whoText: We are a small, independent team. No venture capital, no growth targets, no pressure to monetize your attention. Content App exists because we wanted a reading platform we would use ourselves — calm, honest, and built for the long term.
simple.contactText: Questions, feedback, or ideas? We read every message.

whynoads.title: Why we built Content App without ads
whynoads.excerpt: The web is full of noise. Here's our thinking behind an ad-free reading platform.
whynoads.body:
The web today is full of noise — autoplay videos, popups, tracking scripts. We wanted a reading experience that respects your attention.

That's why Content App has no ads. No banner ads, no sponsored posts, no hidden promotions. Just content.

The trade-off: we rely on reader support. If the platform helps you, consider donating. It's what keeps us ad-free.

bilingualux.title: Designing for bilingual readers
bilingualux.excerpt: How we handled English and Bengali side-by-side - without auto-translation or awkward layouts.
bilingualux.body:
Designing for two languages is harder than it looks. English is compact; Bengali is expressive and uses complex ligatures. A layout that works for one often breaks the other.

We solved this by giving each language its own typography scale, line-height, and spacing. Not just translating strings — but designing for the language's rhythm.

The result: readers in both languages get an experience that feels native, not translated.

ttswebspeech.title: Text-to-speech without an API bill
ttswebspeech.excerpt: How the Web Speech API lets us read articles aloud in two languages - for free.
ttswebspeech.body:
Text-to-speech APIs can cost hundreds of dollars a month. For a small platform, that's a dealbreaker.

We use the browser's built-in Web Speech API. It's free, works offline in many cases, and supports both English and Bengali voices on most modern devices.

Quality varies by device — but for reading articles, it's good enough. And the cost stays at zero.

smallteamshipping.title: What we learned shipping with a tiny team
smallteamshipping.excerpt: Priorities, trade-offs, and the things we said no to.
smallteamshipping.body:
Shipping fast with a small team means saying no — a lot.

We said no to: a mobile app (for now), comments, social sharing, and a dozen shiny features. Every 'no' freed time for the things that actually matter: reliable reading, clean design, bilingual support.

Our lesson: small teams win by subtraction, not addition.

googledriveasdb.title: Using Google Drive as a database (really)
googledriveasdb.excerpt: Why we chose a simple JSON-on-Drive backend for a small content platform.
googledriveasdb.body:
Using Google Drive as a database sounds crazy — but for a small content platform, it's perfect.

No server to maintain, no database to provision, no scaling worry. We store JSON files on Drive and fetch them from the API. Updates are instant. Backups are automatic.

When we outgrow it, we'll migrate. Until then, it's the simplest thing that works.

readingmetrics.title: Reading metrics that actually matter
readingmetrics.excerpt: Percentages, streaks, and why we skip time on site.
readingmetrics.body:
Most reading metrics are vanity. 'Time on site' means nothing if someone left a tab open.

We track three things that matter: did you finish the article? did you come back? did you save something for later?

These three tell us if the content is actually useful — and they respect the reader's privacy.

rules.title: Rules
rules.subtitle: Five principles that keep this platform useful, honest, and calm. By using Content App, you agree to them.
rules.footer: We may update these rules as the platform grows. If you spot a problem, write to us.

kind.title: Be kind
kind.body: Disagree with ideas, not people. Harassment, personal attacks, and hate speech have no place here.

value.title: Add value
value.body: Write things worth reading. No spam, no clickbait, no low-effort posts that waste the reader's time.

honest.title: Be honest
honest.body: Cite your sources. If you quote someone, link to them. Do not claim others' work as your own.

respect.title: Respect the reader
respect.body: No dark patterns, no forced sign-ups, no tracking scripts. The reader is not the product.

privacy.title: Protect privacy
privacy.body: Never share someone else's personal information without consent. What happens in private stays private.
